name: split_line_at_end

name: split_line_beyond_end

name: trim_line_without_intersection

name: split_circle_at_one_position

name: split_arc_at_freecads_position

name: split_arc_on_it

name: split_level_line
note: Its horizontal on the start-side piece only, its length the distance between the outer ends (decision 1, 4d6b1f3eb8): one freedom more, the split point's slide.

name: split_level_line_within_1e-8_of_start
note: A split 1e-8 mm from the start: Silico refuses it (within 1e-7 mm of an end); FreeCAD 1.1.3 makes a 1e-8 mm piece.

name: split_level_line_1e-6_from_end
note: A split 1e-6 mm from the end, past the 1e-7 mm floor: both split.

name: split_line_with_direction_constraints
note: Direction constraints on the start-side piece only (decision 1; 1.1.3 copies them to both, and one is redundant); a perpendicular to a line neither piece touches kept (main drops it).

name: split_line_with_angle
note: An angle on the split line survives on the start-side piece (78e5729520; 1.1.3 segfaults, main's bbbff1f8f1).

name: split_line_points_on_each_half
note: Each on goes to the piece holding its point, the one past the end to the end piece, and the distance to the second piece (bbbff1f8f1; 1.1.3 drops them, #28240).

name: split_line_tangent_symmetric_midpoint
note: The tangent to the piece touching the circle, the symmetric about the start-side piece (decision 2), the midpoint a symmetric of the outer ends.

name: split_line_at_tangent_contact_side
note: The contact at x 3 is on the second piece now: the tangent goes there (decision 2).

name: split_line_at_held_point
note: A split at a point held on the line: the pieces share it, and its on goes (as implied).

name: split_line_tangent_on_second_half
note: A tangent_on onto the split line goes to the piece holding its point, the second (main's findPieceContainingPoint; 1.1.3 not probed by the note).

name: split_arc_keeps_end_tangents
note: Both tangent_ats kept at the outer ends (6d06b61c7e; 1.1.3 makes them coincidences), the radius on one piece.

name: split_circle_with_constraints
note: A circle split at 60 and 240 degrees: the on at 30 and the tangent at 270 degrees go to the second arc, the radius to the first.

name: split_circle_tangent_on
note: A circle split at 10 and 170 degrees: the tangent_on onto it goes to the first arc, counter-clockwise from 10 to 170 degrees, which holds its point at 90 (main's findPieceContainingPoint).

name: trim_away_end_two_share
note: Trimming away an end two other lines share: they keep it, joined to each other (FreeCAD's model has the trimmed line's end as the hub of their coincidences).

name: split_point
note: Splitting a point: Silico refuses it; FreeCAD 1.1.3 segfaults.

name: trim_point
note: Trimming a point: Silico refuses it (5efb8e5e76); FreeCAD 1.1.3 deletes it.

name: remove_point_alone
note: A point no curve uses: deleted on both.

name: trim_line_end_as_drawn
note: testTrimLineSegmentEnd as drawn: FreeCAD joins the new end to the cutter's start (its 5e-5 mm test); Silico gives it a new point on the cutter (decision 5).

name: trim_line_end_held
note: testTrimLineSegmentEnd with the cutter's start held on the line: the line's new start is the cutter's start.

name: trim_line_mid_as_drawn
note: testTrimLineSegmentMid as drawn: two lines, each end at a cut a new point on its cutter (decision 5).

name: trim_line_mid_held
note: testTrimLineSegmentMid with the first cutter's start held: the first piece's end is that point; the second's a new point on the crossing cutter.

name: trim_circle_one_cut
note: testTrimCircleEnd: one cut, so the circle is deleted.

name: trim_circle_mid_as_drawn
note: testTrimCircleMid as drawn: one arc, from the crossing to the cutter's start, each end a new point on its cutter (decision 5).

name: trim_construction_circle
note: testTrimEffectOnConstruction: the arc left is construction, and so are its new points (23ecf94ab6).

name: trim_arc_end_as_drawn
note: testTrimArcOfCircleEnd as drawn: the arc shortened to the cutter's start, its new end a point on the cutter (decision 5).

name: trim_arc_mid_as_drawn
note: testTrimArcOfCircleMid as drawn: two arcs sharing the centre, each end at a cut a new point on its cutter.

name: trim_drops_full_length
note: testTrimEndEffectOnFullLengthConstraints: one end trimmed away, so the length goes (2779f0b29f).

name: trim_drops_symmetric_of_ends
note: testTrimEndEffectOnSymmetricConstraints: a symmetric naming both ends goes when one end does (f0d30cb570).

name: trim_keeps_unrelated_tangent
note: testTrimEndEffectOnUnrelatedTangent: the tangency to the circle that isn't the cutter stays edge to edge (08a66afbc8).

name: trim_worked_example
note: The note's worked example: pieces (0,0)-(3,0) and (7,0)-(10,0), horizontal on both, the length a distance of the outer ends, the second piece's start the cutter's, the first's end a point on the crossing cutter, the point at 9 on the second piece; equal and the point at 5's on dropped.

name: trim_tangent_cutter_becomes_end_tangency
note: The circle cuts where it touches (tangency counts), and the edge tangency becomes an end tangency at the first piece's new end (dec01d1df0, decision 8).

name: trim_circle_at_tangent_contact
note: A tangent line cuts the circle where it touches (3cbe309330): the arc left runs from the crossing at -53 degrees to the contact at 90, where its end takes the tangency.

name: trim_arc_pick_outside_sweep
note: A pick at 315 degrees, outside the arc's sweep: Silico trims at the nearer end, FreeCAD 1.1.3 removes 90 to 180 degrees.

name: trim_arc_between_cuts
note: A pick at 135 degrees: two arcs, 0 to 90 and 180 to 270, sharing the centre.

name: trim_at_centre
note: A pick at the arc's centre: Silico refuses it; FreeCAD 1.1.3 throws.

name: trim_symmetric_about_line_into_two
note: Two pieces, neither of which is the line: Silico refuses the trim, naming the symmetric (decision 2); FreeCAD drops it.

name: trim_symmetric_about_line_shortened
note: One piece, the same line: the symmetric kept (FreeCAD 1.1.3 drops it).

name: trim_arc_tangent_no_piece_touches
note: Two arcs, neither touching the line: Silico refuses the trim, naming the tangent (decision 2); FreeCAD drops it.

name: trim_arc_tangent_contact_removed
note: The contact at 90 degrees is on the part removed (the short line doesn't reach it, so doesn't cut): no piece touches the line, so Silico refuses the trim, naming the tangent (decision 2); FreeCAD drops it.

name: trim_perpendicular_cutter
note: The line trimmed back to the cutter it's perpendicular to: the perpendicular stays (it's between directions, D4), and the new end is a point on the cutter.

name: trim_perpendicular_cutter_into_two
note: The line trimmed between its cuts at x 3 and 6: two pieces, each horizontal; the perpendicular to the upright on every piece (:183).

name: trim_by_construction_line
note: Construction cuts (715f98d1f3): the line trimmed back to x 5.

name: trim_point_does_not_cut
note: A point doesn't cut: no cut, so the line is deleted, and the point's on with it.

name: trim_away_shared_end
note: Trimming away an end the neighbour shares: the neighbour keeps the point and its lock; the line's new end is a point on the cutter.

name: remove_middle_of_chain
note: Deleting the middle of a chain: A and B free; the lock on D's start stays on the point A keeps.

name: remove_batch_with_duplicate
note: A batch with a member named twice: the same as one by one (41c91574cf).

name: remove_constraint
note: Removing a constraint by ID.

name: unjoin_chain_end
note: Unjoining A from D at their shared point: the lock stays with D, which keeps the point.

name: unjoin_unshared_point
note: Unjoining a point no other curve shares: Silico refuses it; FreeCAD's vertex Delete does nothing (bc4d463cdf).

name: remove_hub_of_three
note: Deleting one curve at a three-way joint: the others stay joined (0358ff7ce2).

name: unjoin_one_of_three
note: Unjoining one curve of three: the other two stay joined.

name: unjoin_keeps_length
note: Unjoining A, which has a length: it keeps it (FreeCAD's vertex Delete drops it, 0358ff7ce2).

name: remove_circle_sharing_centre
note: Deleting a circle whose centre two arcs share: the arcs' centres stay one point.

name: remove_point_curves_use
note: Deleting a point curves use: Silico refuses it (decision 7); FreeCAD has no such edit.

name: remove_tangent_neighbour
note: Deleting the arc tangent at a joint of three: its tangent_at goes with it, never onto a neighbour (9ce5756011), and the lines stay joined.

name: unjoin_tangent_neighbour
note: Unjoining the arc: its tangent_at goes, since they no longer meet; the lines stay joined.

name: remove_tangent_on_curve
note: Deleting a line tangent on a circle at an end another line shares: the tangent_on goes with it (1.1.3 leaves a malformed coincidence).

name: unjoin_tangent_on_curve
note: Unjoining the tangent line: its tangent_on goes with it, to its new point.

name: remove_line_with_angle
note: Deleting one of two lines with an angle: the angle goes (e66849378b).

name: remove_symmetric_about_line
note: Deleting a symmetric's about line drops the symmetric (0016d6f2f8).

name: remove_line_with_midpoint
note: Deleting a line with a midpoint whose ends the sides keep: Silico removes the midpoint with its line.

name: merge_touching_ends
note: testSingleMissingCoincidentCase's fix: two ends at one place made one point.

name: merge_touching_ends_other_first
note: The same, the other point kept.

name: merge_line_ends
note: Merging a line's two ends: Silico refuses it; FreeCAD's Coincident command refuses a collapse (#20771).

name: merge_named_twice
note: A point named twice: already one point, refused by both (cb2780e2fa).

name: merge_apart
note: Merging the upright line's top with a loose point 1 mm from it: Silico places it at the loose point, FreeCAD's coincidence is solved.

name: merge_closes_triangle
note: The missing corner's two points made one: a closed triangle.

name: merge_collapses_through_chain
note: Merging a line's two ends through a third point: refused (084379651a).

name: merge_with_constraint_between
note: A horizontal_points between the merged points would name one point twice: Silico refuses; FreeCAD's coincidence makes it redundant, and its command rolls that back.

name: merge_leaves_edge_tangent
note: Merging would leave an edge tangent at a shared end: Silico refuses (decision 8, until open item 13).

name: merge_two_locked_ends
note: Merging two ends each locked at the same place: the locks agree, so Silico merges (its solve keeps redundant constraints that agree); FreeCAD's Coincident command rolls back a solve that finds them redundant.

name: merge_holds_own_point_on_line
note: The sweep's edit_32_490 in small: merging the line's end into a point held on it, 6 mm away, would make the on hold the line's own point on it. Silico's merge refuses that (the own-curve refusal, pending decision 13b of docs/design/m5.0-app.md, #222); FreeCAD's coincidence makes it.
